record.question:
A company creates a VPC with primary IPv4 CIDR 10.232.18.0/24. EC2 instances must resolve records in a Route 53 private hosted zone. Instances assigned public IPv4 addresses must also receive AWS public DNS hostnames. The VPC currently uses a DHCP option set that points to an old custom DNS server with no forwarding for the private zone.

Which two changes meet these requirements using the native VPC resolver? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC and set both enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames to true.
Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC and change the VPC instance tenancy to dedicated.
Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC and enable Network Address Usage metrics.
Associate a DHCP option set whose domain-name-servers value is AmazonProvidedDNS and ensure the instances obtain the updated DHCP settings.
Associate a DHCP option set whose domain-name-servers value is 10.232.18.98 and ensure the instances obtain the updated DHCP settings.

explanation.text:
Options <<1>> and <<4>> configure the DNS service and direct instances to use it. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC and enable both DNS attributes. enableDnsSupport enables Amazon DNS resolution; enableDnsHostnames, together with DNS support and a public IPv4 address, permits AWS public DNS hostnames. Private hosted-zone use also requires both attributes.

The DHCP domain-name-servers value AmazonProvidedDNS points clients at the native Route 53 Resolver. For this VPC, its VPC-relative IPv4 address is 10.232.18.2, the primary network address plus two; the link-local address 169.254.169.253 is also available. Replacing the explicitly unsuitable custom resolver is necessary here, and existing instances must obtain the changed settings.

Option <<2>> changes hardware tenancy rather than DNS behavior. Option <<3>> measures network address utilization rather than enabling DNS resolution or hostnames. Option <<5>> supplies an arbitrary address within the VPC, not the native resolver. A DHCP DNS value does not create a DNS server at that address.

AWS references checked on 2026-09-18:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/AmazonDNS-concepts.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_DHCP_Options.html

diagram_alt: The VPC resolver is the network address plus two, and both DNS attributes, hosted-zone association, and the client resolver settings have distinct roles.

sources.supports: Resolver addresses, both VPC DNS attributes, private hosted zones and public IPv4 hostname prerequisites.
DHCP option sets configure instance DNS servers.

editorial_notes: Added the existing unsuitable DHCP configuration so changing it is a necessary second action. Preserved the two-answer key 1 and 4.
